what_this_measures: Which skill of the family a realistic request actually reaches. All six are loaded at once (claude --plugin-dir agent), so a query can only 'pass' by landing on the right one. A sub-skill query that lands on the umbrella counts as routed, since routing is the umbrella's job.
environment: Run from a checkout of a real iOS application, not an empty directory. In a small or empty repo find and grep answer most single-metric questions correctly and no skill is needed, which measures the fixture rather than the descriptions.
paragon_criterion: A query belongs in a metric skill's positive set only if at least one holds: (a) it spans more than one commit; (b) it needs machine-readable output for a dashboard, report or CI; (c) it has to line up with other metrics on the same commits; (d) the metric's own semantics beat a shell one-liner — inheritance resolved through the SDK for types, cloc's code-versus-comment counting for loc, per-target settings from xcodebuild for build-settings. Otherwise find, grep or wc answers it in one line and Claude declining to consult a skill is correct, not a miss. files and pattern have no (d), so their paragons rest on (a), (b) or (c).
negatives: 24 near-misses that share vocabulary with the family but need something else — an .xcresult bundle, test coverage, a rewrite, dependency updates. None of them may fire a skill.
